title: Shifted simultaneous power-free polynomial values are recurrence parameters exactly at good shifts
theorem: For fixed k>=2 and a finite family F=(f_i) of nonzero integer polynomials, each separable over Q with every nonconstant irreducible factor of degree at most k+2, assume the joint local condition |Omega_p|<p^k for every prime p. Conditional on the pinned 2026 power-free density Corollary 1.3, for every integer r the shifted set A_{F,r}={n>=1:n+r is a simultaneous k-power-free input for F} is an averaging set of polynomial multiple recurrence iff every f_i(r) is k-power-free.
assumptions: The number-theoretic positive-density Euler-product theorem is imported from OpenAI Math Release preprint 020, Corollary 1.3 (24 Sep 2026), and is not externally validated here. The dynamics implication uses Bergelson-Kulaga-Przymus-Lemanczyk-Richter, Definition 1.1 and Theorem 1.4.
proof_mechanism: Finite-prime truncations are periodic and converge to 1_A_F in Besicovitch density because their densities converge to the Euler product; fixed translates preserve this property. For every u, affine dilation f_i(x)->f_i(ux+r) preserves the hypotheses if all f_i(r) are k-free: primes dividing u have no bad residues, and primes coprime to u act bijectively modulo p^k. The density theorem then makes A_{F,r} divisible, hence averaging. If q^k divides any f_i(r), A_{F,r} misses qN and the q-cycle with polynomial t gives zero return average.
supplied_vs_acquired: Supplied: F, k, joint local condition, the cited density theorem, and the established rational-set recurrence theorem. Acquired: periodic approximation, dilation invariance of the local interface, exact iff proof.
costs: Qualitative only. The imported density theorem states an asymptotic but provides no numerical onset in this package; the rationality proof is Cesaro/Besicovitch and the recurrence theorem supplies no effective finite-pattern threshold.
baseline: The source theorem supplies density but not this recurrence criterion. The closest direct dynamics input is Theorem 1.4 for rational positive-density sets.
falsifier: A family meeting all hypotheses and all f_i(r) k-free at a fixed shift r whose translated set fails divisibility, or a family with one non-k-free f_i(r) that is nevertheless averaging, would falsify the iff. The proof reduces either failure to a directly checkable density or cyclic-system calculation.
unresolved: External validation of the 2026 density input, proof-priority review of this transfer corollary, and effective recurrence rates.

title: Same-local-admissibility positive-density quartic family can fail recurrence
theorem: For k=2 the family (x^4+18,x^4+5) is jointly locally admissible at every prime and has positive density of simultaneous squarefree values conditional on preprint 020, Corollary 1.3, yet its parameter set omits 3N and is not an averaging set of polynomial multiple recurrence.
assumptions: The density conclusion is conditional on the same imported power-free-value theorem. Eisenstein irreducibility and the modular obstruction are exact elementary facts.
proof_mechanism: The local conditions are checked symbolically by separating p=2,3,5 and using at most four simple roots per component for p>=7. If 3|n then 9|n^4+18. On the 3-cycle with the singleton set at zero and polynomial t, every parameter correlation is zero.
supplied_vs_acquired: Exact family and imported density theorem supplied; modular root analysis and the cyclic nonrecurrence witness acquired.
costs: A finite exact modular checker covers selected primes; the all-prime condition follows from the symbolic case split in RESULT.txt, not from the checker.
baseline: Positive density alone, and even positive density plus the joint local admissibility condition, do not imply polynomial recurrence.
falsifier: A residue calculation showing a prime p with all classes in Omega_p, or a q-cycle return at a parameter n not divisible by q, would falsify the record.
unresolved: The 2026 density input remains a preprint premise; no external validation or novelty claim is made.

title: Irrational polynomial phases are Cesaro-orthogonal to the shifted power-free set
theorem: Under GN2-01's density hypotheses, for any fixed good shift r and any fixed real polynomials Q_1,...,Q_m such that every nonzero integer combination has an irrational nonconstant coefficient, the normalized sum N^{-1} sum_{n<=N, n in A_{F,r}} exp(2 pi i sum_j h_j Q_j(n)) tends to zero for every nonzero h in Z^m.
assumptions: The power-free family is Besicovitch rational conditional on the pinned density Corollary 1.3. Weyl equidistribution for each fixed irrational polynomial phase is imported standard input.
proof_mechanism: Replace the indicator by a fixed periodic approximant. Split into residue classes modulo its period and apply Weyl to each affine-substituted phase; then let the Besicovitch approximation error tend to zero.
supplied_vs_acquired: Supplied: density theorem and Weyl criterion. Acquired: the periodic-weight transfer for this family of polynomial-value sets.
costs: Qualitative Cesaro convergence only; no uniformity in the phase coefficients, shrinking Bohr sets, or finite-prefix onset.
baseline: A direct consequence of Besicovitch rationality and Weyl equidistribution; the theorem is a scoped application, not a new equidistribution principle.
falsifier: A fixed phase vector meeting the Weyl irrationality condition with nonzero Cesaro correlation against a good-shift indicator would falsify the record.
unresolved: External verification of the 2026 density input and any effective uniform phase-distribution rate.
